correctness.rationale: The exact published hazard was differentiated. In the both-subunit shape quadrant the derivative is negative through the point where the exponential-power derivative changes sign. Beyond that point, the ratio of the positive exponential-power derivative to the magnitude of the negative Weibull derivative has a strictly positive logarithmic derivative on the full domain. The ratio rises from zero to infinity, proving one and only one derivative zero. Endpoint limits make that critical point the unique global minimum. The packaged checker independently confirms the formulas and the source Figure 2(b) scale separation.

evidence: Standard exponential-power references document a hazard proportional to a power times an exponential-of-power term and its ability to be bathtub-shaped.
Generalized and additive Weibull papers establish flexible hazard classes for different models, but their functional forms are not the FEPW competing-risk sum used here.
The FEPW theorem requires proving that adding a decreasing Weibull component preserves exactly one eventual upturn; that implication is supplied by the new monotone-ratio proof.

value.rationale: Hazard-shape flexibility is a central motivation of the FEPW model and is highlighted in the abstract and dedicated Figure 2. The result replaces an entire advertised decreasing-hazard quadrant by an exact unique-bathtub classification and explains why the source's finite plots nevertheless look decreasing. This is a global structural correction relevant to reliability interpretation, not a narrow numerical discrepancy.
